title: Fix tokens/sec calculation for streaming responses (align on first-token timestamp)
author: Omar El-Sayed
release_notes: Fixes tokens/sec for streaming requests by computing decode-rate starting at first-token timestamp (avoids canary false positives driven by prefill/queue time).
description:
Context: During perf-canary prototyping we noticed a consistent discrepancy between runtime logs and the aggregated tokens/sec metric for streaming endpoints. The existing tokens/sec implementation used request_start_ts as the denominator start time for both streaming and non-streaming. For streaming, this effectively bakes in queue + prefill + time-to-first-token into the tokens/sec calculation, which makes decode throughput look worse (and noisier) than it is. This caused at least two canary panels to show apparent throughput regressions during warmup / cache priming when TTFT moved but decode stayed flat.

Change summary: Update tokens/sec calculation for streaming responses to align the measurement window to the first-token timestamp (TTFT) instead of request start. For streaming responses, we now compute tokens/sec as (generated_token_count / (last_token_ts - first_token_ts)) with guardrails for 0/negative durations and the 1-token case. Non-streaming continues to use (request_end_ts - request_start_ts) because it represents the full end-to-end duration.

Details / semantics: (1) We define first_token_ts as the timestamp when the first token is actually emitted to the streaming transport (i.e., the first chunk flush), not when the decode loop starts. (2) If the stream produces 0 tokens (error/early abort), tokens/sec is not emitted. (3) If duration_ms <= 0 (clock skew / missing timestamps), we drop the sample and emit a debug counter. (4) For exactly 1 token, we compute tokens/sec using (request_end_ts - first_token_ts) to avoid division-by-near-zero spikes; this matches how we interpret a 1-token stream (first token == last token) but the stream still has meaningful time on wire.

Why this is correct for canary: The canary’s throughput detector is intended to catch decode throughput regressions (kernel/scheduler/batching/kv-cache interactions). TTFT and queue time are important, but they should be tracked separately (we already chart p95 TTFT and p95 end-to-end). Folding TTFT into tokens/sec was conflating signals and producing false positives when TTFT moved due to unrelated scheduler changes.

Tests: Adds unit tests for streaming and non-streaming tokens/sec with a fake monotonic clock, including edge cases (1 token, missing first_token_ts, and negative duration). Adds an integration-style test to ensure the streaming transport path sets first_token_ts when the first SSE chunk is flushed.

Rollout/metrics: This is a behavioral fix for an internal metric. It will change the absolute tokens/sec values shown for streaming workloads (expected to increase vs previous). I added a temporary dashboard note (tracked in ENG-2845) to avoid confusion when comparing week-over-week charts.

Notes: This PR does not change any customer-facing API behavior. It only affects internal metric computation and the canary’s regression detector inputs.
commits: metrics: record first_token_ts on first streaming chunk flush
metrics: compute streaming tokens/sec from first_token_ts to last_token_ts
tests: add tokens/sec unit coverage for streaming edge cases
telemetry: add debug counters for dropped/invalid tokens/sec samples
docs: inline comment clarifying tokens/sec semantics for streaming vs non-streaming
conversation: Nadia Rahman (review): Can we confirm first_token_ts is the timestamp at emit-to-transport, not decode-start? For canary we want the transport-aligned definition so TTFT and tok/s are consistent. Also please add a guard for the 1-token stream case; otherwise tok/s can explode.

Omar El-Sayed (author): Yep—updated SSE writer to set first_token_ts on the first chunk flush (previously we only had decode_start_ts). Added guardrails: drop duration<=0, and for exactly 1 token use (end_ts - first_token_ts). Added tests for both.
Noah Patel (review): This looks right. One nuance: for dropped samples, we should emit a counter so we can see if we’re losing data silently. Also please ensure non-streaming path is unchanged.
Omar El-Sayed (author): Added redwood_metrics_tokensec_dropped_total{reason=...} and verified non-streaming codepath is untouched (test asserts exact behavior).

Sean Gallagher (review): This will shift tok/s up; please call that out in the release note / PR description so oncall doesn’t interpret it as an improvement regression. Also: any impact on alert thresholds in the perf-canary detectors?

Omar El-Sayed (author): Added note in description + release note. Canary detectors are being tuned this week; I pinged ENG-2845 owners and added a dashboard annotation note request. No paging impact expected until thresholds updated.
Logan Wright (review): Thanks. One more: make sure metric label schema is unchanged (we had a cardinality budget discussion).
Omar El-Sayed (author): Confirmed: no new labels. Only changed how the value is computed + added a debug counter with fixed labels (reason enum).
Nadia Rahman (approval): Approved once CI is green.
